method: All nine exact original PNGs were opened through view_image in three batches and actually viewed. No regenerated, cropped or edited image was used.

findings.observation: At 960x540 the complete seven-column board, Back/Pause, saved-turn status and seven input controls are visible without text overlap. The Lumo figure is visible to the right.

At 2400x1080 the result menu visibly scrolls vertically and initially clips the next action at its own viewport edge. Header, result status and seven disabled column controls remain separate and legible.
Pause modal clearly shows the saved-round message and Continue/New round/Play against Lumo. Background move controls and Pause are visibly disabled.
At 1080x2400 the cyan move and gold response occupy the same center column, with the cyan turn shown next. The board, seven controls and header remain visible.

At 1080x2400 the whole 7x6 board and all seven column controls are visible; Back/Pause and saved-turn status are legible. The board occupies the portrait width with substantial vertical space above and below.
At 1080x2400 the result modal shows the win, three actions and seven disabled column controls without text overlap. The translucent modal intentionally obscures the board.

At 640x360 the result menu has a visible vertical scrollbar; only the first action is in the initial viewport. Header and result status remain legible. Lower menu actions require scrolling; this still image alone does not prove that interaction.

At 320x740 all three result actions are legible and separate. The seven-column button row intentionally exceeds the narrow viewport and has a visible horizontal scrollbar; columns beyond the right edge require scrolling. No claim that all seven are simultaneously visible.
Four cyan pieces and their winning outline are visible in the bottom row; the status says Cyan wins and the menu button is available.

result: No blocking visual issue identified in these nine still images. Scroll-dependent layouts are explicitly recorded rather than described as fully visible.
limits: These are desktop Godot runtime captures at specified viewport sizes, not Android device screenshots.
No device FPS, Android navigation, save integrity or touch interaction is inferred from still-image viewing.
The other 250 frame images were not manually reviewed by Root in this pass.
The full current C4 workflow is still running; this record does not declare whole-candidate acceptance.
